verses.author: model_A
verses.text: An orchard planted by a man who never tasted its fruit.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the grafted branch forgets
whose hands first bent it toward the sun

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
spring rain finds
the old scars in the bark
still green underneath

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
someone's boot prints
filling with rainwater
between the rows

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a crow counts them
step by step, then flies off
without telling anyone

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the empty rows
keep the shape of walking
long after the boots are gone

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
morning fog erases
even that shape—
someone still walks it by memory

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the field forgets first
the body forgets last—
still turning at the same row's end

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a lantern left burning
in a window no one opens—
still, moths find their way there

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the moths don't know
the light was ever for someone—
they only know it's there

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a road remembers weight
long after the wheels are gone—
grass grows crooked telling it

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
someone else's shovel
still fits my hand strangely well—
the dirt doesn't ask whose

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
rain fills the print anyway—
no boot needed to call it a puddle

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I leave the door unlatched
for a wind that doesn't need permission—
it comes in like it lives here

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the cat already knew this—
sleeping in the spot the sun will choose
before the sun arrives

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
morning takes attendance
without me—
the coffee still answers to my name
